name: Room 7
narrativeOnEnter: A small room. A bare mattress on an iron frame. The barred window is painted over. The walls are covered in scratched writing — the same four digits, repeated hundreds of times.

action.text:
CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT FILE
Patient 07 — Blackwood Psychiatric Institute

Full name: VOSS, ELARA — formerly Dr. E. Voss, Neuroscientist
(Previous affiliation: [REDACTED — see AXIOM restricted file])
Admission: March 14th, 1972 | Involuntary
Ward B — Room 7
Diagnosis: 'Persecutory ideation, non-compliant disposition'
(Diagnosis issued on recommendation of AXIOM Group — see attached referral)

Treatment notes:
— 'Therapeutic EEG sessions' scheduled weekly. Duration: 90 min.
— Patient is uncooperative. Physically restrained for sessions.
— Neural mapping quality: EXCELLENT (AXIOM notation, appended to file).

Dr. Harlan's handwritten note at the bottom:
'Admission number assigned per standard protocol.
Gate combination = admission month + day reversed.
4-0-3-1

I know what she used to be before they sent her here.
She was a neuroscientist. She refused to work with AXIOM.
So they had her committed and mapped her anyway.

She was right about everything she accused us of.
I'm writing this down. When she gets out — and I intend to let her — 
I want there to be a record that she told the truth.'

Second note, different ink, weeks later:
'She got out last night. I didn't tell anyone.
God forgive me for waiting this long. — H'

Scratched into the plaster, over and over, by something sharp and patient:

4031 4031 4031 4031 4031
4031 4031 4031 4031 4031

And among them, other words, written in layers over months:
'THEY CHANGED THE LOCK'
'I KNOW THE CODE'
'I WILL GET OUT'

'MY NAME IS ELARA VOSS'
'I WAS A SCIENTIST BEFORE THEY MADE ME A PATIENT'
'I REFUSED TO HELP AXIOM MAP NEURAL PATTERNS WITHOUT CONSENT'
'SO THEY HAD ME COMMITTED AND DID IT TO ME ANYWAY'

'THERE ARE 47 OF US IN WARD B'
'THEY CALL IT THERAPY'
'IT IS NOT THERAPY'
'WE ARE DATA TO THEM'

'RECORDS VAULT — DIRECTOR — MASTER KEY — 1972'
'THE TRUTH IS IN HARLAN'S FILES'
'AXIOM GROUP — PROJECT HELIOS — PHASE 1'
'WE WILL NOT BE FORGOTTEN'

At the very bottom, in much smaller, steadier handwriting — different from the rest:

'She got out. I watched her go.
— Agnes Colm, Ward B Nurse, November 1972'

Four thick iron bars. The glass behind them is painted over in grey. You can't see outside.

One of the bars has been worked at — there are scratch marks in the paint — but it hasn't moved.

A bare mattress, stained and worn. Beneath it, a small hollow has been carved into the floorboards — not quite empty.

A torn scrap of paper, missed in the dark:

It's a list. Names. 47 rows, handwritten small. Some crossed out. Some circled. One name at the top is underlined:
'VOSS, ELARA — Patient 07 — Neural map session 1 complete.'

Each entry is stamped: 'AXIOM — HELIOS Phase 1 — confirmed.'

At the bottom, in Voss's handwriting:
'They mapped all of us. Every session. 90 minutes in a chair.
They told us it was therapy.
I know now what it was for.
They're building something from what they took.
I don't know what.
But I will find out.
And when I do — I will make them answer for every name on this list.
— E. Voss'
